brief: Ahead of SpaceX's Q3'26 print, Goldman Sachs refreshes its AI segment forecasts on the back of new hosting deals, public disclosures and model progress, raising AI segment revenue estimates to ~$27.3bn (FY26), ~$90.4bn (FY27) and ~$146.7bn (FY28), reiterating Buy and raising its price target to $230 from $220. The raise rests on two legs: compute capacity (visibility to ~2.4GW by YE26, ~7.0GW by YE27, ~10.6GW by YE28, driven by power/cooling, datacenter shells and GPU supply) and monetization (short-term hosting deals at ~$40-50bn+/GW, long-term floor ~$20bn/GW), which together imply current Street estimates are under-modeled and could see 9-31% upside through FY28. Orbital compute stays out of estimates through YE28, scaling only from 2029. Supporting context: Starship's Flight 14 succeeded, management announced a $100bn Starbase LA facility, and consumer metrics are mixed (Starlink MAU growth decelerated to 21% YoY from 63% in Q2, while X and Grok app growth inflected positive). Key risks flagged: governance concentration in the Founder/CEO, and AI segment reliance on unproven orbital datacenter technology.
